result:
Solution 3 matches the exponent I recall for this problem, and its derivation is a heuristic that I checked only for internal consistency.

Solution 1 claims the LLF walk is as destructive as possible, keeping only the cut points, which gives α = −1/2. Cut points survive every erasure order, so −1/2 is only a lower bound on α. Solution 1's argument that contacts "almost always kill" is not justified.

Solution 2 claims LLF has the same exponent −1/3 as chronological loop erasure. It offers no real argument, and the two procedures treat loops very differently, so there is no reason for the exponents to agree.

Solution 3 uses the four-dimensional square-root rule for non-intersection of two paths. It reproduces the known chronological exponent −1/3 (b = (1−b)/2) and the cut-point exponent −1/2 for two raw arms. For LLF, both arms are already thinned at larger scales, so survival is a two-sided non-intersection of two LLF paths. That gives b = (1−2b)/2, so b = 1/4 and α = −1/4. This also fits my recollection that the expected LLF loop-erased walk length in four dimensions is n(log n)^(−1/4+o(1)), but I did not verify that from a source.

CHOICE: 3
